text:
julian: Security asked for a tighter flow around privileged change exports — specifically who can download presigned bundles. we need a proposal for both API scopes and console UX.

maya: +1. Current export links are presigned S3 URLs with 24h validity. Security wants an approval step for any 'privileged' export (role-based and with justification).

sam: what's our definition of 'privileged' here? exports that include actor PII / full request/response payload / admin-only routes?

dana: I'd say: any export that contains unredacted actor identifiers or full request/response bodies should be privileged. metadata-only exports (timestamps, action types) can stay normal.

julian: agree with dana. Also they want audit trail for the download itself (who clicked the link, IP, when) and the ability to revoke a presigned link after creation.

leah: UI-wise: show an 'Export for privileged data' checkbox that triggers a modal: requester must pick justification + select approver (or auto-assign to oncall). That creates an export in PENDING state.

maya: for API we can add a new scope `audit:export:privileged` and two endpoints: POST /exports (same body) returns export_id with status PENDING, and POST /exports/:id/approve. Approve requires reviewer token + reason.

julian: ops-bot: can you create a quick diagram with states? PENDING -> APPROVED -> READY (link created) -> DOWNLOADED -> REVOKED.

ops-bot: created diagram gist: https://internal.gist/priv-export-states (ops-bot) :white_check_mark:

sam: question: if we hold off on generating presigned link until APPROVED, we avoid stale links, but we need an async job to build the bundle on approval. That could add latency. acceptable?

dana: acceptable if we show ETA and can optionally generate a small sample while bundle builds. We should also allow short-lived (1h) links and immediate revocation.

maya: also need to handle exports requested via API by service accounts (automation). Those should flow through an ACL/automation-approval policy, not manual.

julian: good call. add `automation_approval_required` flag on tenant settings. For enterprise tenants, default to manual.

leah: telemetry: include export.requested_by, export.approved_by, approval_latency_ms, bundle_build_time_ms, link_ttl_seconds, download_count, last_download_ts. Send events to audit-stream with tag `export:privileged` so SIEM can pick them up.

julian: about retention of export artifacts — legal requires exports containing PII to be retained for 90 days then auto-deleted unless tenant opts in. who owns deletion?

dana: storage will lifecycle-delete via S3 lifecycle + audit service will mark export.deleted_ts. Add a console column 'Retention expiry'.

maya: redaction modes: we should support three modes: redacted (actor IDs hashed), pseudonymized (actor alias), unredacted (privileged). Only users with `audit:export:privileged` can request unredacted.

sam: implementation plan (rough): backend: add ExportModel.flag_privileged, approval queue, jobs to build bundle and generate presigned link, revoke API; console: modal + approver picker + audit details; auth: new scope and RBAC mapping; telemetry: new events; infra: lifecycle policy + retention metadata.

julian: can someone sketch the API shape?

maya: sample: ```POST /v1/exports { "query": "...", "fields": ["action","actor_id","payload"], "redaction": "unredacted|pseudonymized|redacted", "privileged": true, "justification": "legal request" }``` Response 202 with export_id. Approve: `POST /v1/exports/{id}/approve { "approver": "leah", "reason": "ok for legal" }` then webhook on READY.

leah: I want an auditsvc-bot message on approval and on download: `auditsvc-bot: export {id} approved by {user} at {ts}` and `auditsvc-bot: export {id} downloaded by {user} from {ip}` so security can subscribe.

auditsvc-bot: noted. will emit events to audit-topic and create a retention tag.

sam: LD: need to think about rate limits + quotas. privileged exports are heavy — we should have separate quota bucket and soft cap with billing alert. Also approval SLA (24h?) for manual approvals — default to 8h for enterprise.

dana: plus an on-call fallback: after SLA, can auto-approve to avoid blocking customer workflows but only if tenant has agreed. record this in justification.

maya: edge-case: user approves an export then wants to revoke link later. we must preserve proof of revocation in the audit trail.

julian: action items: 1) maya + sam draft API and RBAC mapping (EOD Wed). 2) leah + dana wire up modal + approver UX (mock by Thu). 3) ops to add lifecycle + revocation hooks (ops-bot assign). 4) auditsvc to add events (auditsvc-bot).

leah: I'll own the UX copy for justification templates. keep them short: "Legal subpoena", "Investigative request", "Internal review".

ops-bot: created tasks: infra#1234 export-lifecycle, auth#1235 audit-scope, ui#1236 privileged-export-modal.

julian: thanks all — this is the shape we'll present in next PM sync. :eyes:
